rules.rule: When a run stops at its --stop-after limit, leave the checkpoint on disk.
When a run stops at its --stop-after limit, do not write the final output.
Do not run `pip install` inside a loader container attached to the noorinalabs_backend network at runtime; deps must be baked into the image at build time.
Run the staging loader container attached to the noorinalabs_backend docker network.
Never commit Neo4j secrets or passwords to the repository.
Use /tmp rather than /home/deploy for writing files on the staging host.
Apply loads to production only with explicit owner sign-off.
When a node keying change means the loader will not MERGE, delete the existing nodes and then load to avoid stale duplicates.
Run a cross-corpus deduplication audit on the Shia content before cutting over to production.
When A/B-testing a fix against a base ref, swap the file content (e.g., with git show <ref>:<path>) rather than using git stash.
When regenerating the structural ontology index locally, run `python3 scripts/structural_ontology.py emit`, not `uv run python …`.
To see real data, use a local Docker Neo4j instance instead of the staging box.
Re-verify `docker info` when container work suddenly fails, since Docker WSL integration can silently revert.
Do not spend wave time trying to enable Docker-in-WSL2; treat it as an environment/owner action outside scope.
Do not use an edge-connectivity query to check whether Chain nodes are populated.
Verify Chain node population by checking `c.chain_length` or `size(c.narrator_ids)`.
To recover/resume a crashed disambiguate run, use `resolve --from-step disambiguate` so NER is skipped and the existing narrator_mentions_resolved.parquet is reused verbatim.
Do not use a bare `resolve` re-run to resume a crashed disambiguate run, since it regenerates NER mention_ids and forces a cold start of the checkpoint.
To determine whether two names merge, run `_can_merge` instead of relying on a lexical heuristic.
Before implementing ENGINE_CHANGEs or strategy rewrites, present the design for user review and do not write code until it is reviewed.

For any significant code change (new strategy logic, engine modifications, multi-file refactors), use EnterPlanMode or present a structured plan, and wait for approval before launching go-architect or writing code.
Verify the filer CIKs in sec/filer_config.go against live EDGAR before using them in production.
To backfill 13F filings, run `go run ./cmd/omo-backfill-13f` with `--from-quarter` set to the starting quarter and `--user-agent` set to a company name and contact email.
When the IB Gateway login screen is stuck, check that TWS_USERID and TWS_PASSWORD are set in .env.
When the multi-account selector dialog blocks auto-login on IB Gateway staging, log in with the paper-specific login staging100 instead.
Only rebuild omo-core when Go source code changes.
Never run omo-data as a local tmux process.
When manually triggering omo-data, use `docker compose run --rm omo-data --run-once`.
Delegate downloads, model pulls, and other human-executable tasks to the user instead of running them via Bash.
Before making any change, check whether a GitHub issue already exists for it by running `gh issue list --repo vipulbms/crypto-trader-agent`.
Investigate and confirm the root cause before creating a GitHub issue or making a fix.
Run the full test suite before committing, and ensure all tests pass.
Save all tests, regardless of who writes them, in the `tests/` folder so they can be found, rerun, and extended in future sessions.
Never write test logic as inline `python3 -c` scripts when validating a real feature; write it to `tests/test_<feature>.py` instead.
Before executing a git commit, prepare the commit message for review, unless the user says "commit" directly or invokes /commit.
When making any code or config change, consult this project context to understand the full system.
The /commit skill must never stage .env, data, or logs files.
Only execute a commit when the user asks for it.
When the user opens agent.log, read it to diagnose the issue.
Leave the user's fork branches in place.
Delete fork branches only when the user explicitly requests it for that specific case.
Reclaim the on-disk build/ and vendor/ duplicates of a retained branch or worktree, while keeping the branch ref and tracked diff.
Before implementing any new SNES ROM in the compiler stress-test battery, read docs/snes-demo-cookbook.md.
Rebuild the toolchain from the committed patches by running dev/run.sh toolchain.
When de-XFAILing a stale XFAIL, make no compiler change.
Use dev/regen-patch.sh to verify the worktree against the committed patches.
When tearing down a feature or investigation worktree, never delete the core scripts used to determine results.
Retain a worktree until its work merges upstream.
Reclaim a kept worktree's build/ and vendor/ duplicates without removing the worktree itself.
Treat a worktree's build/ directory as always safe to delete, since it contains only compiled output.
